items.stem: In Wp(n,Σ), the parameter p represents:
items.explanation: The parameter p gives the dimension and order of the random Wishart matrix.

items.stem: In the defining sum of n independent normal outer products, the Wishart degrees of freedom are:
items.explanation: Each independent normal vector contributes one outer product, so the degrees of freedom equal n.

items.stem: The Wishart matrix formed from outer products is always:
items.explanation: Each outer product ZZ′ is symmetric, and sums of symmetric matrices are symmetric.

items.explanation: The degrees of freedom equal the number of independent vectors, which is five.

items.explanation: The matrices are independent and share scale Σ, so their degrees of freedom add to seven.

items.explanation: Estimating the sample mean uses one degree of freedom, leaving n−1 for the sample covariance matrix.

items.stem: Which statements about the Wishart distribution are correct?
items.explanation: A, B and C are true. D is false because the dimension is p, while n counts independent vectors.
statements: The degrees of freedom count independent normal vectors.
The scale matrix is their covariance matrix.
The matrix dimension always equals the degrees of freedom.

A.why: The defining sum is a sum of symmetric outer products.

B.why: Each independent vector contributes one degree of freedom.

C.why: The common covariance matrix is the Wishart scale.

D.why: The dimension p and degrees of freedom n are distinct parameters.

items.stem: Independent W₃(2,Σ) and W₃(5,Σ) are summed. The expectation of the result is:
items.explanation: The sum has seven degrees of freedom, and its expectation is seven times the common scale matrix.

items.stem: The sample mean vector and sample covariance matrix are independent when the observations are:
items.explanation: The independence of the sample mean and sample covariance is a classical result under multivariate normal sampling.

items.stem: For nonsingular Σ, a Wishart matrix is positive definite with probability one when:
items.explanation: With enough independent normal vector contributions to span p dimensions, the matrix is positive definite with probability one.

items.stem: June 2026 Q17: two independent whitened four-dimensional X vectors and three independent whitened four-dimensional Y vectors are combined. The result is:
items.explanation: The first whitened block contributes W₄(2,I₄) and the second W₄(3,I₄). Their independent sum is W₄(5,I₄).

items.stem: Which statements give the conditions for adding two independent Wishart matrices by adding their degrees of freedom?
items.explanation: A, B and D are correct: the matrices must be independent, share the same scale matrix and have the same matrix dimension. Equal degrees of freedom are not required; they are added.
statements: The two Wishart matrices are independent.
They have the same scale matrix.
They must have equal degrees of freedom.
They have the same matrix dimension.

A.why: Independence is required for the standard Wishart addition property.

B.why: A common scale matrix is required so the two Wishart distributions belong to the same scale family.

C.why: Their degrees of freedom may differ; the resulting degrees of freedom are their sum.

D.why: Both matrices must have the same order to be added as members of the same Wishart family.

items.explanation: Whitening transforms the scale matrix to identity while preserving dimension four and degrees of freedom nine.

items.stem: If (n−1)S~W₂(8,Σ), then the original sample size n is:
items.explanation: The Wishart degrees of freedom are n−1=8, so the sample size is n=9.

items.stem: Which statements about the sample covariance Wishart result are correct?
items.explanation: A, B and D are true. C is false because the result is not Wp(n,Σ) when the mean is estimated.
statements: nS follows Wp(n,Σ) for the usual centred sample covariance.
The sample mean and S are independent.

A.why: The classical exact Wishart result assumes multivariate normal observations.

B.why: The sample covariance uses n−1 degrees of freedom.

C.why: The usual sample covariance is centred at the estimated mean, costing one degree of freedom.

D.why: Under multivariate normality, the sample mean and sample covariance are independent.
